quick_brief: Challenge of the second week: Test your skill in programming animated objects (ImageSprite), activating voice control and converting sound into readable and audible texts!

questions.text: What animated object should be placed inside Canvas to display animated and interactive images such as shooting games?
Which programming event is executed automatically as soon as the user's finger touches an ImageSprite element?
Which property do we use to make the ImageSprite object automatically move at a specified speed without stopping?
What is the invisible tool that uses Google's engine to convert the user's audio pronunciation and speech into written text?
Which command do we use to instruct a smartphone to speak and read text written in a clear human voice?
In the game Catching the Cat, to randomly change the location of the cat, we use a function to generate a random number:
Which event is called automatically in the voice recognizer just after the user has finished speaking and the text is available?
To update the score and increment it by 1 each time the player hits the target, we write the equation:
options: set global score to (get global score + 1)
set global score to (get global score * 1)
questions.correct: set global score to (get global score + 1)

questions.text: What is the appropriate tool (Component) to cause a slight vibration in the phone (Vibrate) when a certain button is pressed, such as in fighting games?
Which property determines the angle and direction of movement of the animated cat within the Canvas?
Write code to automatically move an object named CatSprite to random coordinates X=150 and Y=a random number from 1 to 300 when touched.
questions.correct_code:
when CatSprite.Touched (x, y)
do call CatSprite.MoveTo (150, random integer 1 to 300)

questions.text: Write the code to launch the speech recognizer SpeechRecognizer1 immediately after the user clicks on the speak button called Button_Speak.
